cards.definition: To say what another person said, using your own words.
cards.example:
- placeholder
placeholder
- He paraphrased her objection so accurately that she relaxed immediately.
Ele parafraseou a objeção dela com tanta precisão que ela relaxou na hora.
- A short paraphrase buys you five seconds to think before you commit to anything.
Uma paráfrase curta te dá cinco segundos para pensar antes de se comprometer com qualquer coisa.
cards.note: Diferente de rephrase, que é reformular o que você mesmo disse: parafrasear é devolver o que o outro disse. O substantivo é a paraphrase e o passado, paraphrased. A fórmula pronta em reunião é So what you're saying is…

cards.definition: To ask further questions in order to get past the first, easy answer.
cards.example:
- placeholder
placeholder
- She probed a little further and found the real reason for the delay.
Ela aprofundou um pouco mais e encontrou o motivo real do atraso.
- Probing questions dig deeper without ever sounding like an interrogation.
Perguntas de aprofundamento cavam mais fundo sem nunca soar como interrogatório.
cards.note: Probing questions são as perguntas que cavam mais fundo sem virar interrogatório. Como substantivo, a probe é uma investigação formal. Colocações frequentes: probe further, probe into something.

cards.definition: Something you accept as true without checking it first.
cards.example:
- placeholder
placeholder
- We were working on the assumption that the budget had already been approved.
Estávamos trabalhando na suposição de que o orçamento já tinha sido aprovado.
- Her question exposed an assumption the whole team had shared for months.
A pergunta dela expôs um pressuposto que o time inteiro compartilhava havia meses.
cards.note: O verbo é assume, que não significa assumir a culpa — isso é take responsibility. Colocações fortes: challenge an assumption, make an assumption, work on the assumption that.

cards.definition: To make something easier to understand by explaining it better.
cards.example:
- placeholder
placeholder
- Could you clarify what you mean by “as soon as possible”?
Você poderia esclarecer o que quer dizer com “o mais rápido possível”?
- The email clarified nothing, so we ended up calling the supplier.
O e-mail não esclareceu nada, então acabamos ligando para o fornecedor.
cards.note: O substantivo é clarification e o pedido educado é Could you clarify…? Em reunião, Just to clarify… é a forma menos agressiva de apontar uma contradição.

cards.definition: A clear and useful understanding of how something really works.
cards.example:
- placeholder
placeholder
- The interviews gave us valuable insights into why customers leave.
As entrevistas nos deram percepções valiosas sobre por que os clientes vão embora.
- A good coach offers insight, not advice.
Um bom coach oferece percepção, não conselho.
cards.note: Colocações: gain an insight, share an insight, insights into something. Não confunda com inside, que é dentro. Também funciona como incontável, sem artigo: that gave me real insight.

cards.definition: A tendency to favour or reject something, often without noticing it.
cards.example:
- placeholder
placeholder
- Confirmation bias makes us hear only what confirms the plan we already like.
O viés de confirmação nos faz ouvir só o que confirma o plano de que já gostamos.
- The panel was biased towards candidates from the same university.
A banca era tendenciosa em relação a candidatos da mesma universidade.
cards.note: Unconscious bias, o viés inconsciente, é o tema mais citado em treinamentos de contratação. O adjetivo é biased: a biased decision. Colocações: bias towards e bias against.

cards.definition: To understand a meaning that is suggested but never said directly.
cards.example:
- placeholder
placeholder
- If you read between the lines, that email was a very soft refusal.
Se você ler nas entrelinhas, aquele e-mail era uma recusa bem educada.
- He never read between the lines, so the hint was completely wasted on him.
Ele nunca leu nas entrelinhas, então a indireta foi totalmente desperdiçada com ele.
cards.note: Essencial em negociação e em feedback educado demais. É expressão fixa: nada de read between lines nem read in the lines. O passado se escreve igual, read, mas soa como o adjetivo red.

cards.definition: To return to a point that was mentioned earlier in the conversation.
cards.example:
- placeholder
placeholder
- Before we close, I want to circle back to Marina's objection about the scope.
Antes de encerrarmos, quero voltar à objeção da Marina sobre o escopo.
- We circled back to the pricing question at the very end of the call.
Voltamos à questão do preço bem no fim da ligação.
cards.note: Mostra que você guardou o que a pessoa disse, sinal claro de escuta ativa. Vem sempre com to antes do assunto: circle back to that point. Passado: circled back to. Sem complemento, diga let's circle back later.

cards.definition: Needing to be handled with care because it can upset people.
cards.example:
- placeholder
placeholder
- Salaries are a sensitive subject in any restructuring.
Salários são um assunto delicado em qualquer reestruturação.
- He was sensitive enough to notice that she was uncomfortable.
Ele foi sensível o bastante para notar que ela estava desconfortável.
cards.note: Cuidado com sensible, que é sensato: a sensitive subject e a sensible decision são coisas diferentes. Para dados, o par fixo é sensitive information. O advérbio é sensitively.

cards.definition: Specific, and not just any one of a group.
cards.example:
- placeholder
placeholder
- Was there a particular reason for cancelling the workshop?
Havia um motivo específico para cancelar o workshop?
- She is very particular about how the minutes are written.
Ela é muito exigente com a forma como a ata é escrita.
cards.note: “Uma conversa particular” é a private conversation; particular, em inglês, é específico. In particular significa em especial. Com about, o adjetivo muda de sentido e passa a ser exigente: particular about details.

questions.prompt: A client explains a problem in three long sentences. Which move counts as paraphrasing?
options: Repeating the client's point in your own words.
Saying your own idea again in a clearer way.
Asking the client to explain the whole thing again.
Writing the client's exact words in the minutes.
questions.answer: Repeating the client's point in your own words.
questions.explanation: To “paraphrase” is to give back what the other person said, in your own words.

questions.prompt: She challenged one _____ and the whole business case fell apart.
questions.explanation: An “assumption” is something taken as true without being checked.

questions.prompt: Com clientes educados demais, você precisa ler nas entrelinhas.
questions.answer: With overly polite clients, you have to read between the lines.|With very polite clients, you need to read between the lines.
questions.explanation: To “read between the lines” is to catch the meaning that was only suggested.

questions.prompt: Layoffs are coming and the subject needs careful handling. Which sentence is correct?
options: Layoffs are a sensible topic, so let's be careful.
Layoffs are a sensitive topic, so let's be careful.
Layoffs are a sentimental topic, so let's be careful.
Layoffs are a sensational topic, so let's be careful.
questions.answer: Layoffs are a sensitive topic, so let's be careful.

questions.prompt: Deixe-me esclarecer dois pontos antes da votação.
questions.answer: Let me clarify two points before the vote.|Let me clarify two points before we vote.
questions.explanation: To “clarify” is to make a point easier to understand.

questions.prompt: When a client says everything is “fine”, that is exactly when you should _____.
questions.explanation: To “probe” is to ask further questions instead of taking the first answer.

questions.prompt: In Portuguese, “uma conversa particular” is a private conversation. So what does “a particular concern” mean?
questions.explanation: “Particular” means specific; the Portuguese “particular” is “private” in English.

questions.prompt: If we still have time at the end, I would like to _____ your point about hiring.
questions.explanation: To “circle back to” something is to return to a point raised earlier.

questions.prompt: Ela compartilhou um insight que mudou toda a nossa estratégia.
questions.answer: She shared an insight that changed our whole strategy.|She shared an insight that changed our entire strategy.
questions.explanation: An “insight” is a deep, useful understanding of how something works.

questions.prompt: In a hiring panel, what does “unconscious bias” describe?
options: A rule that stops managers from hiring their friends.
A method for scoring every candidate on paper.
A question designed to test a candidate's honesty.
A preference you act on without ever noticing it.
questions.answer: A preference you act on without ever noticing it.
questions.explanation: A “bias” is a leaning for or against something, often outside your awareness.
